result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_k_edge_connected()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if an undirected graph stays connected after removing any `k - 1` edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L40547-L40606){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_k_edge_connected(k) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is k-edge-connected](/assets/graphs/is-k-edge-connected.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same six-node cycle on both sides. Left: removing any single edge leaves a path, so the cycle is 2-edge-connected and is_k_edge_connected(2) returns True. Right: removing the two accent edges B–C and E–F splits it in two, so fewer than 3 edge removals disconnect it and is_k_edge_connected(3) returns False." width="100%"} A graph is k-edge-connected when it has more than `k` nodes and no set of fewer than `k` edges disconnects it; equivalently, every pair of nodes is joined by `k` edge-disjoint paths. 1-edge-connected means connected, and 2-edge-connected means connected without bridges. Use it to check that a network tolerates a given number of link failures. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The number of edges that must be removed to disconnect the graph (at least 1). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is k-edge-connected. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `k` is less than 1 or the graph is directed. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} As in NetworkX, the graph needs at least $k + 1$ nodes and minimum degree at least $k$ (quick rejections); otherwise it is k-edge-connected exactly when all nodes form a single k-edge-connected component (see `k_edge_components()`). ## Examples {.doc-examples} A cycle survives any single edge failure but not two; a complete graph on five nodes survives any three: ::: {#43df7888 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ring = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(6) k5 = ec.Graph().add_full_graph(5) ring.is_k_edge_connected(2), ring.is_k_edge_connected(3), k5.is_k_edge_connected(4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False, True) ``` ::: :::
